question: to the Commission Bert-Jan Ruissen (ECR), Kris Van Dijck (ECR) Subject:

The inland waterway transport sector is crucial for smooth and more sustainable logistics. Transport by water produces fewer emissions per tonne of freight than road transport. The sector is aiming for a 40 to 50 % reduction in CO₂ emissions by 2030 and for zero emissions by 2050. For this reason, inland waterway transport will fall under the EU ETS2 system from 2028, in addition to RED III. Essential to the 2030 targets in particular is the availability and affordability of, among other things, HVO (hydrotreated vegetable oil). However, this fuel for inland waterway transport has become significantly more expensive in 2026, with prices reaching as high as EUR 1 400 per 1 000 litres – almost three times as expensive as conventional diesel. According to media reports123, this price hike, which is partly a consequence of the new RED III Directive and the discontinuation of BIDO tickets (which previously kept prices down for inland waterway transport), makes sustainable navigation using HVO less attractive. According to RTV Noord4, some businesses, such as the ferry service to the Wadden Islands in the Netherlands, are already reverting to fossil fuels. 1.
Does the Commission share the concern that efforts to make inland waterway transport more sustainable may stall in the short term due to this sharp rise in the price of biofuel?
If so, what solution does the Commission propose?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (1.6.2026) The Commission would like to recall that the provisions in Article 25 of Directive (EU) 2018/20011 (as amended) set targets for the uptake of renewable energy across the transport sector, aiming at reducing overall greenhouse gas emissions. To that regard, there are no specifications per individual transport mode and Member States have flexibility in how to achieve the objectives. Accordingly, it is for the Netherlands to decide within this framework, whether to allow for the cross-subsidisation of HVO (hydrotreated vegetable oil) supplies to certain sectors through schemes such as BIDO tickets. The Commission remains committed to support the decarbonisation of the transport sector. On 5 November 2025 it adopted the Sustainable Transport Investment Plan (STIP) (COM(2025) 664 final2), which aims to de-risk investments in the production of renewable and low-carbon fuels and to increase their availability for the aviation and waterborne sectors, including the inland navigation sector. Increased supply is expected to contribute to lower costs over time for all relevant sectors.
